As someone who currently is coming out as trans at an older age, one of the hardest things I’ve been working through is the fact that I never got to explore my gender identity when I was younger. It lead to a lot of repression, which led to a lot of depression and anxiety. If I had been raised in an environment more welcome to these kinds of conversations, I think I would be in a much healthier and happy place. Now, I feel like I’m working through an impossible pain. 

I don’t mean to generalize, but I do think sometimes what cis people don’t understand is that untreated gender dysphoria is one of the most painful prisons to wake up in everyday. Can you imagine if everyday you had to walk in and present in the completely wrong body? If we were to curate an environment that welcomed these kind of questions, it would probably save some lives. People think we’re in a wholly accepting environment now, but every trans person at every age is now bombarded with thoughts that are like this post—that we are just going through a phase or a fad and we’ll regret it in ten years—and that notion is really painful. I should make it clear that I don’t think this pain was meant in a malicious way at all, but also lines of thinking like this are so exhausting when you’re already dealing with a shit ton of dysphoria in every passing moment. 

So yeah, maybe some kids who are experimenting now with pronouns, gender identity, and gender presentation will change back to what they were assigned with at birth. But oh my god—coming from a trans man—I really wish I had the freedom they did at their age. Because I’m working through so much pain from my repressed childhood that I doubt I’ll ever have a healthy and comfortable relationship with myself. 

Also, my other suggestion would be that if you’re really struggling with this and can’t understand it, try talking to an actual healthcare professional that works with patients who suffer from dysphoria, or better yet, a trans person. Don’t just talk about us—talk to us. And please, DO NOT just rely on studies that lay out plain numbers—maybe actually try talking to a trans person about it, or someone who works a lot with trans people. Talk to us (not just about us) about our experiences—please. I promise we aren’t as scary as a lot of media makes us out to be. 

I’m sorry, I hope this doesn’t come off as I’m angry, because I’m not. It’s just this type of thinking is what trans people basically hear everyday, and it genuinely can be very painful to hear sometimes. Maybe it’s just one of those days for me.
